activity.notes: Po'pay, a Tewa religious leader from Ohkay Owingeh, coordinated the 1680 Pueblo Revolt and exercised cross-pueblo leadership after the Spanish expulsion. ATLAS uses Pueblo Coalition as an explicit editorial identity for the temporary multi-pueblo political-military coalition, not as a claim that the culturally diverse Pueblo peoples formed a permanent unified nation-state. Archaeological scholarship places Po'pay out of power by late 1681, so the end boundary is approximate.

sources.title: Mission San Juan Bautista — National Park Service
sources.citation_text: The National Park Service identifies Po'pay as a religious leader from Ohkay Owingeh and a major organizer of the 1680 Pueblo Revolt that expelled the Spanish from New Mexico for twelve years.

sources.title: The Other American Revolution: Archaeology and the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 — Harvard Peabody Museum
sources.citation_text: Harvard archaeologist Matthew Liebmann describes Po'pay's coordination of the revolt across multiple Pueblo communities and notes that he was out of power by late 1681.
